To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hnRNP G has two independent RNA binding sites that are both important to regulate SMN2 exon7 splicing.
hnRNPG binds to the SMN2 exon7 and is essential for the recruitment of the trimeric complex of Tra2-β, hnRNPG and SRSF9.
hnRNPG RRM binds to SMN2 pre-mRNA and this interaction is required for its splicing activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanism of hnRNP-G-mediated regulation of the splicing of exon 7 of SMN2.
the characterization of the hnRNP G RNA recognition mode and with its role in the regulation of the SMN2 exon splicing, which is crucial for SMA patients.
the characterization of the RNA recognition properties of hnRNP proteins and their role in the regulation of splicing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hnRNP-G binds to the polyA tract upstream of the Tra 2-β1 site and is required to stabilize the Tra2-ß1/hnRPN G/SRSF-9 complex on exon 7.
Tra2-β and hnRNP G act in concert to activate the inclusion of SMN2 alternative exon 7.
hnRNP-G is a crucial component of the SMN2 splicesome.

The main takeaway from our work is that
hnRNP G has a major role in SMA exon 7 spicing and is a potential target for SMA therapy.
hnRNP-G is a major player in the splicing regulation of SMN2 and that it is recruited to exon 7 by a specific interaction with a polyadenine tract.
hnRNP proteins can regulate splicing in multiple ways and that they can act as both positive and negative regulators.
